name: Cristal Otero

bio.statement: Otero's voters' pamphlet statement lists a background in homeless services and city and county government.
bio.excerpt: Homeless Services; City and County Government

bio.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement lists an MSW from Portland State University, an MA from Pacific Northwest College of Art and a BA from The Evergreen State College.
bio.excerpt: MSW, Portland State University; MA, Pacific Northwest College of Art; BA, The Evergreen State College

bio.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement lists service as a Mark O. Hatfield Fellow with the City of Fairview and as a senior program specialist in Multnomah County homeless services.
bio.excerpt: Mark O. Hatfield Fellow, City of Fairview; Program Specialist Senior, Homeless Services, Multnomah County

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Otero has eight years of direct-service experience with homeless residents.
bio.excerpt: Otero has eight years of experience working in direct service with homeless residents

positions.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Otero says she will judge major projects and borrowing by their monthly cost to Portlanders.
positions.excerpt: I will judge major projects and borrowing by what they cost Portlanders each month.

positions.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement says Portland should set a goal to end homelessness for people with intellectual disabilities and brain injuries.
positions.excerpt: Portland should set a concrete goal: end homelessness for people with intellectual disabilities and brain injuries

positions.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement proposes letting some publicly supported apartment buildings transition to resident ownership and management.
positions.excerpt: some publicly supported apartment buildings can transition to resident ownership and management

positions.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement says she will back prevailing wages, apprenticeships and labor standards on public projects.
positions.excerpt: I will back prevailing wages, apprenticeships, safe working conditions, and labor standards on public projects.

positions.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement says the Portland Clean Energy Fund should fund climate work, not budget gaps.
positions.excerpt: PCEF should fund climate work, not budget gaps.

positions.statement: Otero's pamphlet statement says she will reduce seismic risk at the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub.
positions.excerpt: I will reduce seismic risk at the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Otero says she wants to expand housing production while giving neighborhoods more say over its speed, style and density.
positions.excerpt: I want to expand housing production while giving neighborhoods more say over the speed, style and density of change;

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Filing form name 'Cristal A Otero'; ran in 2024 as 'Cristal Azul Otero' (OPB 2024 profile title in search results).
